input.narrative: To Whom It May Concern, My name is XXXX XXXX, and I am writing regarding restrictions currently preventing me from opening a personal banking account with U.S. Bank. During that period, my personal information and accounts were compromised as part of a broader identity theft situation that affected multiple financial institutions and credit accounts. As a result, my U.S. Bank account was ultimately closed due to the fraudulent activity associated with the compromise. Since then, I have spent years working to resolve these issues through law enforcement reports, FTC identity theft filings, attorney representation, and direct disputes with creditors and financial institutions. I greatly appreciate the time and professionalism of the branch staff, and I am simply asking for an opportunity to move forward. I am very interested in building a long term relationship with U.S. Bank both personally and professionally. I own and operate XXXX XXXX XXXX, an XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX business based in XXXX XXXX. My business generates substantial annual revenue approaching XXXX XXXX, and I would like to transition both my personal and business banking to U.S. Bank so I can take advantage of the products and services your institution offers.

input.narrative: To Whom It May Concern, I am submitting this complaint regarding unauthorized XXXX transactions and Truist Banks failure to properly respond after receiving direct and timely notice of fraudulent activity involving my account. This matter involves unauthorized electronic fund transfers associated with my Truist business account for Chills on XXXX XXXX, as well as My personal checking account. I did not initiate, authorize, or knowingly benefit from any of the disputed XXXX transactions. Critically, Truist received actual notice of fraudulent activity before additional transactions were allowed to proceed. On XX/XX/year> at approximately XXXX AM, after receiving an alert regarding a XXXX transaction that I did not authorize, I immediately contacted Truist Fraud Services. I remained on the phone with Truist for approximately 16 minutes and 55 seconds. During that call, I specifically informed Truist that : * I did not authorize any XXXX transactions, * My phone and/or account access had been compromised, * I was out of the country at the time, * No XXXX transactions should be processed or paid. Truist informed me on that call that my accounts would be frozen and not to worry about any transactions being processed. Despite this direct warning from me, and the assurance from TRUIST all fraudulent unauthorized XXXX transfers were inadvertently processed after this date. Further, on XX/XX/year> at approximately XXXX PM, I again contacted Truist regarding the ongoing fraudulent activity and remained on the phone with Truist for approximately 26 minutes. During this second call, I again reported unauthorized activity and attempted to stop additional fraudulent transactions. The unauthorized XXXX transactions include, but may not be limited to, the following : * XX/XX/year> XXXX Payment to XXXX XXXX ID XXXX {$920.00} * XX/XX/year> XXXX XXXX to XXXX XXXX ID XXXX {$920.00} * XX/XX/year> XXXX XXXX to XXXX XXXX ID XXXX {$3000.00} * XX/XX/year> XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Payment ID XXXX {$3000.00} * XX/XX/year> XXXX XXXX to XXXX XXXX XXXX ID XXXX {$3000.00} * XX/XX/year> XXXX XXXX to XXXX Payment ID XXXX {$500.00} * XX/XX/year> XXXX XXXX to XXXX Payment ID XXXX {$600.00} * XX/XX/year> XXXX XXXX to XXXX Payment ID XXXX {$1000.00} * XX/XX/year> XXXX XXXX to XXXX Payment ID XXXX {$1500.00} * XX/XX/year> XXXX XXXX to XXXX XXXX ID XXXX {$1200.00} * XX/XX/year> XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Payment ID XXXX {$1000.00} These transactions total approximately {$16000.00} in unauthorized XXXX transfers, exclusive of additional related fraudulent activity and fees constitute unauthorized electronic fund transfers under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( EFTA ) and Regulation E ( 12 CFR 1005 ). Despite : * timely fraud reporting, * sworn affidavits, * direct warnings to Truist, * and ongoing communications regarding compromised access, Truist denied reimbursement and improperly characterized these transactions as authorized. I am requesting : 1. Immediate reimbursement of all unauthorized XXXX transfers, 2. Immediate issuance of any outstanding provisional credit required under Regulation E, 3. A complete reinvestigation of all disputed transactions, 4. Production of all records relied upon in denying the claims, including IP logs, device information, authentication records, internal notes, and fraud investigation materials, 5. Written explanation of how Truist concluded these transfers were authorized despite prior notice of fraud and explicit requests to stop payment activity. This complaint concerns unauthorized account access and failure to adequately respond after actual fraud notice was provided. I reserve all rights and remedies available under federal and state law.

input.narrative: I am submitting this response to formally and aggressively dispute your false and unsupported claim that my previous request was not submitted by me. This assertion is inaccurate, negligent, and appears to be an intentional tactic to avoid your legal obligations. This dispute was filed directly by me, the consumer, and not by any third party. I am not working with any credit repair organization, credit counseling agency, or outside company of any kind. Your repeated use of a generic, scripted responsewithout conducting an actual investigationconstitutes a blatant violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). Under FCRA 611 ( 15 U.S.C. 1681i ), you are required to : - Conduct a reasonable investigation of all disputed information - Review all relevant evidence I submit - Provide the method of verification, including : 1. The name and contact information of the furnisher 2. The method used to verify the disputed information 3. Copies of all documents relied upon Your continued refusal to process my dispute, despite receiving proper documentation, is not only unlawfulit demonstrates clear negligence, bad faith, and repeated non-compliance with federal consumer protection statutes. To eliminate any excuse for your failures, I have provided full identity verification, including my government-issued ID and proof of address. You now have no legitimate or lawful reason to deny or dismiss my dispute. Your repeated closures of my disputes with identical, copy-and-paste language is unacceptable, unlawful, and a direct violation of your duties under federal law.

input.narrative: I had some clothing items I was hoping to sell on XXXX. I listed some items and quickly started seeing some interest. While on the screen to enter my bank info, a chat window popped up. The person on the chat made themselves out to be assisting with the bank verification process and asked me to authorize a test transaction to confirm the account details. They said the transaction would be a small, nominal fee that would then be returned to my account once the account was verified. The small, nominal amount was almost {$700.00}. After a few minutes I knew I had been scammed. I logged off of the chat and contacted my bank to ask them to stop the transaction. My bank denied my fraud claim after completing their investigation. I have requested the documents used in the claim and I'm awaiting them by mail. I have since seen others online with similar issues. We think we are setting up a XXXX sellers account and instead a company named XXXX XXXX scams us out of our money. And banks are allowing this to happen.

On XX/XX/year> I deposited a Truist-issued check for {$11000.00} from a law firm 's XXXX XXXX Account XXXX XXXX local Truist branch in XXXX, FL. Despite this being a Truist-issued check deposited into a Truist account, the bank placed an administrative hold on the entire amount citing " confidential information that indicates the check may be returned '' with no further explanation. In XX/XX/year> I deposited a {$10000.00} check from the same law firm at the same bank with zero issues and funds were released same day. My account has been open since XX/XX/year> with no negative history. I attempted to call the branch directly and received no answer. I called customer care and the representative was unable to locate the deposit in their system despite me having a physical receipt in hand. Truist then sent me an email stating the deposit had " posted '' which was misleading as the funds remained completely unavailable and still showed as an administrative hold. I later learned the hold was triggered by suspicious activity on the law firm 's Truist account a situation completely unrelated to me or my deposit. I am an innocent customer caught in Truist 's internal fraud flag with no clear communication, no assistance from customer care, and no access to my funds despite having a valid receipt and email confirmation from Truist themselves. Funds are scheduled to be released XX/XX/year> but I am filing this complaint due to Truist 's poor communication, misleading notifications, and failure to provide adequate customer service.

I opened an account with Synchrony bank and sent XXXX XXXX as deposit to the account. I then tried to wire money to another account ( {$3500.00} ) after being told by a banker it was ok to do so. I waited a while to hear something back about the money that was being held in the account. Never heard anything back so I started calling Synchrony bank. I was told to have the sender request the funds back. After trying to contact the sender I was told that they can not request casino winnings back after they have been paid out. I called my bank and told them what I was told and they said it was policy. I have called multiple times and at this point Synchrony bank is just holding the money and refusing to send it to me.

I am submitting this complaint regarding a fraudulent Citibank credit card account ( ending in XXXX ) that was opened in my name without my knowledge or authorization. The balance associated with this account is approximately {$9000.00}. For nearly a year, I have been attempting to resolve this matter directly with Citibank and my primary bank, XXXX. On XX/XX/year>, I formally emailed Citis Executive Response Unit requesting that the fraud investigation be reopened after Citi concluded that I was responsible for the account. The individual who opened the Citi account also gained unauthorized access to my XXXX bank account and used it to make payments toward the fraudulent Citi account. Initially, I did not realize the charges appearing on my XXXX account were connected to a fraudulent Citi account because I was not immediately attentive to the statements. Once I became aware of suspicious activity, I promptly contacted XXXX and Citi to investigate the charges and protect my accounts. XXXX investigated the unauthorized debits and determined that the activity was fraudulent. XXXX reversed the charges and reimbursed my account. I provided Citi with documentation from XXXX confirming that my XXXX account had been compromised and that the related transactions were unauthorized. Despite this, Citi concluded that I was responsible for the account because statements were mailed to my address, payments originated from my XXXX account, and my phone number contacted Citi regarding the account prior to the fraud reporting date. These facts do not establish that I opened or authorized the account. The XXXX account used to make payments had itself been compromised, a fact confirmed by XXXX investigation. Further, any calls I made to Citi were part of my efforts to understand suspicious charges and investigate unauthorized activity appearing on my accounts. Once it became clear that the Citi account was fraudulent, I disputed the account and requested that it be closed. I also informed Citi during recorded calls with its fraud department that my XXXX account had been compromised. During XXXX conversation, I was advised by a Citi representative not to close my XXXX account during the investigation. I followed Citis direction in good faith. I believe Citi failed to conduct a reasonable investigation by disregarding Chases fraud findings and failing to adequately evaluate the evidence I submitted. I am requesting that Citi reopen the investigation, review all supporting documentation and recorded calls, and remove the fraudulent account from my credit reporting if Citi can not produce verified proof that I opened or authorized the account.

'' I believe I was racially profiled by the bank and a note was placed on my account by the bank teller. I have an FHA-insured mortgage serviced by Shellpoint Mortgage Servicing . Prior to our hardship, we had never made a late payment on this loan. Our hardship began in XX/XX/XXXX when I lost my job and my spouse, a XXXXXXXX XXXX, was furloughed during a XXXX XXXX. We entered a mortgage forbearance in XX/XX/XXXX and complied with all requests from the servicer during the loss mitigation review process. Our forbearance is scheduled to end on XX/XX/XXXX. During multiple communications with Shellpoint representatives, including our single point of contact and escalation staff, we were verbally informed that the only loss mitigation option available to us was a XXXX loan modification with an estimated monthly payment between approximately {$2500.00} and {$2800.00} depending on resolution of an escrow issue involving lender-placed flood insurance. Our gross household income is approximately {$4200.00} per month. The proposed payment would consume approximately 59 % to 66 % of our gross monthly income and is not affordable or sustainable. Despite repeated requests, Shellpoint has not provided us with a written loss mitigation determination explaining : which FHA waterfall options were evaluated, why other available FHA options were denied, the calculations used, or a complete breakdown of the proposed modification terms. We specifically requested written evaluation and explanation regarding : Combination Loan Modification and Partial Claim, Payment Supplement, XXXX loan modification options, and all other FHA loss mitigation options required under HUD guidelines . We were verbally told that we were not evaluated for some of these options, but no written explanation or eligibility analysis was provided. We also requested a complete itemization of approximately {$8300.00} in fees and advances that Shellpoint stated would be capitalized into the modified loan balance, increasing the balance to approximately {$300000.00}. No itemized accounting has been provided. In addition, a representative stated that certain options were not being offered because using them now could prevent us from receiving assistance again in a future hardship 10 to 15 years from now. We believe this explanation is inconsistent with HUD loss mitigation requirements and may have improperly influenced the review process. On XX/XX/XXXX, we submitted a formal written appeal requesting : a complete written loss mitigation determination, individualized reasons for denial of each FHA option, an itemized fee breakdown, confirmation that foreclosure activity would not proceed while the review and appeal remain pending, and clarification regarding any forbearance extension. As of the filing of this complaint, we still have not received a complete written determination or adequate explanation of the FHA waterfall evaluation conducted on our loan.

Filed a dispute with Wells Fargo for a photoshoot. At my initial shoot, a tip was accidentally submitted. The merchant acknowledged this in writing via email and promised to credit it back. When XXXX XXXX transitioned away from Wells Fargo, I followed all the steps to move to the new XXXX XXXX card and elected to transfer my balance. The XXXX email I received specifically stated : " If you choose to transition to the new XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX, you'll be able to transfer any balance from your old Wells Fargo account. You may also close down your Wells Fargo account. '' It also said : " If you choose to keep your Wells Fargo account open, the old account will become an XXXX XXXX card with a different card number. '' Based on this, I understood that the XXXX conversion would only happen if I chose to keep the Wells Fargo account open. I did not choose that. I chose XXXX XXXX and elected to transfer my balance. Despite that, Wells Fargo automatically converted my old XXXX XXXXXXXX into a Wells Fargo XXXX XXXX XXXX that I never requested, activated, or used. My balance of {$4400.00} was supposed to transfer to the new XXXX card but instead stayed on the XXXX card. Wells Fargo sent all notices to my old address, so I had no idea this account existed until a debt collector called me. I paid the {$4400.00} immediately. I have XXXX on all my cards and have never missed a payment anywhere. I disputed the late fees and interest since they only exist because Wells Fargo sent notices to the wrong address on an account I never asked for. Wells Fargo waived part of the charges but refused to waive approximately {$35.00} in remaining interest. That {$35.00} has now ballooned to {$120.00} from additional late fees and interest on a closed account, while my complaint was still active. Nobody told me charges would keep accruing during the dispute. In their formal response, Wells Fargo tries to put the blame on me. They say it was my responsibility to keep my address updated. But I had no reason to update my address with Wells Fargo because I did not know this account existed. I had already transitioned to XXXX XXXX and updated my address with XXXX. They also say the conversion " did not require individual customer authorization, '' which means they converted my account into a completely different credit card product without my consent. This directly contradicts what XXXX told me. XXXX said the XXXX conversion would only happen if I kept the Wells Fargo account open. Wells Fargo says it happened regardless. What XXXX told me and what Wells Fargo actually did were XXXX different things, and I was caught in the middle. I went through Wells Fargo 's internal complaint process twice ( XXXX XXXX : XXXX ) and got the same denial both times. Their own representative agreed on the phone that this was a blunder, but the formal response calls the partial waiver a " courtesy '' and says no error was found. I told them I would escalate to the CFPB. They did not respond. I am asking Wells Fargo to waive the remaining {$120.00}, confirm the account is closed at XXXX, not report anything negative to the credit bureaus, and provide {$500.00} in compensation for the time and distress this has caused. Thank you for your time and kind attention!

input.issue: Attempts to collect debt not owed
input.narrative: I am submitting this complaint because Fair Collections & Outsourcing is reporting a fraudulent {$160000.00} apartment-related debt on my credit reports. I do not owe this debt, did not open or authorize this account, did not sign a lease or rental agreement for this debt, and believe it resulted from identity theft. I previously had my identification stolen and reported identity theft. Fair Collections & Outsourcing was previously notified in 2023 of my identity-theft issue regarding another fraudulent debt from the same general time period. I provided proof at that time, and the prior fraudulent debt was removed. This newly reported {$160000.00} debt appears to be from the same identity-theft window, yet Fair Collections & Outsourcing reported it to the credit bureaus anyway. Fair Collections & Outsourcing was able to locate my current address for collection and reporting purposes, but appears to have failed to review or connect its own prior records showing that I had already reported identity theft and that another fraudulent debt from the same period had previously been removed. I believe this shows a failure to conduct a reasonable investigation before reporting this debt and a failure to maintain reasonable procedures for handling identity-theft accounts. I am also concerned because Fair Collections & Outsourcing has previously been involved in legal action related to similar issues involving identity-theft debt collection and credit reporting practices. Given that history, the company should have known to investigate this matter carefully before reporting a large apartment-related debt as mine. This reporting is causing serious harm because the balance is extremely large and is damaging my credit profile. input.product: Money transfer, virtual currency, or money service
input.narrative: CFPB Complaint ( https : XXXX ) Company -- Wells Fargo Product/Service -- Savings Account Issue -- Wire Transfer Fraud I am submitting this complaint against Wells Fargo regarding a XXXX {$4500.00} wire transfer from my savings account that occurred after Wells Fargo was already aware my account had been compromised. On XX/XX/year>, I received a notification from Wells Fargo regarding a transaction I did not recognize. I went in person to a physical Wells Fargo branch after receiving notice of suspicious activity on my account. At the branch, I discovered there were three unauthorized transactions totaling {$9600.00}. I disputed all three, and Wells Fargo acknowledged fraud by stopping and reversing those three transactions the same day. Wells Fargo also changed my account number but did not fully secure the account or move the funds because it was after close of business. When I returned to the Wells Fargo branch on XX/XX/year>, to complete the opening of a new account, I was informed of the {$4500.00} wire transfer. I did not authorize that wire transfer. I immediately disputed it and asked why the account had not been frozen despite Wells Fargo already knowing the account was under attack. Wells Fargo had actual notice that my account was compromised, acknowledged that fact by reversing other fraudulent activity, yet failed to place a hard hold or other effective protection on the account. As a result, a large wire transfer was allowed to bypass security overnight. Wells Fargo told me the wire transfer was authorized by a code sent to my phone. I never received any code from Wells Fargo, and my phone was never out of my possession. I also filed a police report regarding this event with the XXXX XXXX XXXX Department on XX/XX/year>, under Report # XXXX. Wells Fargo has denied my claim by stating that a one-time passcode was sent to the phone number on file and used to authorize the transaction. I dispute that explanation. I never received any one-time passcode, and I did not authorize this wire transfer. Wells Fargo has also failed to produce the specific technical information that would support its conclusion, including items such as the IMEI or SIM card ID tied to the alleged authorization. Without producing that evidence, Wells Fargo has not adequately supported its denial. Desired Resolution I am asking the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau to request Wells Fargo to : 1. Explain why it failed to place a hard hold or freeze on my account after I reported the compromise in person at a branch on XX/XX/year>. 2. Explain why it allowed a {$4500.00} wire transfer to proceed overnight after already reversing other fraudulent transactions the same day. 3. Explain why it treated that wire transfer as authorized when I never received any verification code and my phone never left my possession. 4. Produce the complete XXXX XXXX XXXX relied on to deny my claim, including : the exact phone number the code was sent to, the precise timestamp of the message, the IP address or Device ID of the phone that entered the code. 5. Produce any related device, SIM, IMEI, authentication, and authorization records connected to the transaction. 6. Conduct a proper investigation. 7. Reimburse the {$4500.00} taken from my account without my authorization. Thank you. XXXX XXXX XXXX CELL : XXXX e-m : XXXX ========================================================= XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX

I called the fraud department FIVE separate times trying to resolve the issue : First call : verified my information and was told they would call back the phone number on file to unlock the account. No callback ever came. Second call : explained that no callback was received. They reconfirmed the correct number and again promised a callback. Nothing happened. Third call : asked whether there was any alternative verification method. I was told to provide the last 6 digits of the bank account linked for payments. Unfortunately, modern financial tools like XXXX use virtual account numbers for privacy and security, which the representative clearly did not understand. After explaining this, the representative disconnected the call. Fourth call : after already spending hours trying to resolve this, I was told the only remaining option was to mail a verification letter. No urgency, no explanation of what fully locked actually meant, and no attempt to expedite the process. Fifth call : I manually relinked my bank account outside XXXX and successfully made a payment to prove the account was valid and active. Despite this, I was told that because the letter process had already started, the account was now completely locked and nothing else could be done except wait up to 10 business days. This entire situation highlights a massive failure in both technology and customer service. In 2026, there is absolutely no reason a bank should be incapable of securely verifying a customer through an app notification, text message, biometric confirmation, or any modern authentication method. Instead, the process was repetitive, inconsistent, uninformed, and ultimately useless. Do better.

input.narrative: A fraudulent Booking.com hotel reservation in the amount of {$530.00} was placed on my Barclays account for a stay at the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX in Virginia on XX/XX/year>. Additionally, any merchant records reflecting use by XXXX XXXX would further confirm that the transaction was not authorized by me. I am requesting that Barclays : Reopen and properly reinvestigate the dispute ; Provide all documentation relied upon in denying the claim ; Reverse the charge and restore the disputed credit. I believe Barclays failed to conduct a reasonable investigation into this unauthorized transaction.

On XX/XX/year>, I submitted a CFPB complaint against Starmark Financial LLC regarding an alleged debt being reported and/or collected in my name. Attached to my complaint was a formal debt validation and accuracy dispute requesting competent documentary evidence necessary to verify the legality, ownership, accuracy, completeness, and lawful reporting of the alleged account. In my dispute, I specifically requested : the original signed agreement or contract, proof of ownership and assignment, the purchase agreement or transfer records, a complete accounting and payment history, the Date of XXXX Delinquency ( DOFD ), the date the account was charged off, the date the account was assigned or acquired by Starmark Financial LLC, and documentation necessary to verify the accuracy and completeness of the information being furnished to consumer reporting agencies. Starmark Financial LLC responded to the complaint and provided limited account documentation. However, the response failed to fully validate the alleged debt or fully address the reporting accuracy and completeness concerns raised in my dispute. Specifically, Starmark Financial LLC failed to provide : XXXX. The Date of First Delinquency ( DOFD ) associated with the alleged account ; XXXX. Documentary proof substantiating the DOFD being used for credit reporting purposes ; XXXX. The actual charge-off date for the account ; XXXX. A complete delinquency and payment progression history ; XXXX. The purchase agreement, bill of sale, or complete chain-of-title documentation establishing ownership of the account ; XXXX. The original signed agreement or contract bearing my signature ; XXXX. A complete accountin g history showing all payments, fees, adjustments, interest, and balance calculations ; XXXX. Documentary evidence authorizing Starmark Financial LLC to furnish, verify, update, or report information concerning my credit file ; XXXX. A detailed explanation of the procedures and methodology used to investigate and verify the disputed information after receiving my dispute. Although Starmark Financial LLC appears to have asserted that the account was verified, the company did not explain : what records were reviewed, whether original creditor records were examined, whether the investigation involved manual review or automated verification, or how the disputed information was determined to be accurate and complete for furnishing purposes under the FCRA. Providing limited account records or summaries does not fully establish lawful ownership, enforceability, complete reporting accuracy, or compliance with the Fair Credit Reporting Acts reasonable investigation requirements. Additionally, without the DOFD and charge-off date, I am unable to independently verify whether the account is being reported within the lawful reporting period required under the FCRA and Metro 2 reporting standards. Because Starmark Financial LLC continues furnishing and/or verifying this account despite failing to fully provide the requested documentation and verification, there remains substantial concern regarding : the adequacy of the investigation conducted, the accuracy and completeness of the furnished information, and Starmark Financial LLCs compliance with FCRA 1681s-2 ( b ). The account therefore remains formally disputed as inaccurate, incomplete, insufficiently verified, and unsupported by complete documentary evidence.

input.narrative: Formal Request for Reinvestigation and Supporting Documentation for CitiCards Case XXXX To Whom It May Concern, I am writing regarding dispute case number XXXX involving merchant XXXX XXXX XXXX and a disputed charge in the amount of {$16000.00}. I am formally requesting : Immediate confirmation that this dispute has been reopened for investigation ; Copies of all documentation relied upon in determining that I am responsible for the charge ; Copies of any communication allegedly received from the merchant stating that a refund would be issued ; Confirmation of whether any refund transaction was ever actually processed to my account. Timeline of Events : I placed an order with XXXX XXXX XXXX over the phone. I was charged {$16000.00} despite the expected amount being {$1600.00}. I never received the product, order confirmation, shipment confirmation, tracking information, or any subsequent communication from the merchant. After numerous unsuccessful attempts to contact the merchant directly, I filed a dispute with my credit card company. I was later informed that the dispute had been closed and that I was responsible for the charge. On XX/XX/XXXX, I contacted customer service to understand why the dispute was denied. The representative informed me that the investigator allegedly contacted the merchant and that the merchant stated they would issue a refund. I explained during that call that : I had not received any refund ; I had not received any communication from the merchant ; The merchant had been nonresponsive throughout this matter, which was the reason I filed the dispute initially. The representative agreed to reopen the dispute and advised that it could take approximately 710 days to appear reopened on my account. During that same call, I also specifically requested copies of the documentation relied upon by the investigator, including : whom they contacted, when they were contacted, whether there was written communication, any confirmation numbers, emails, invoices, signed authorizations, or any objective evidence supporting the determination that I was responsible for the charge. On XX/XX/XXXX, after still not seeing the dispute reopened, I called again. I reiterated that : I was still being held responsible for the {$16000.00} charge ; my payment due date was approaching on XX/XX/XXXX ; and I still had not received any supporting documentation. The second representative also reviewed the matter and acknowledged that there did not appear to be objective evidence provided by the investigator supporting the determination that I was responsible for the charge. I again asked for the objective evidence supporting the determination to be provided. She again advised that it could take 710 days for the dispute reopening to appear on my account. She additionally referenced that I allegedly did not complete an intake form ; however, failure to complete an intake form is not objective evidence that : I authorized a {$16000.00} transaction, I received the product, or that the merchant fulfilled the order. As of today, XX/XX/XXXX : the dispute still does not appear reopened, I remain responsible for the charge, I have not received any product, I have not received any refund, I have not received any supporting documentation, and I have not received any communication from the merchant. I am therefore formally requesting : written confirmation of the current dispute status ; a reinvestigation of this matter ; copies of all evidence relied upon in the original determination ; and confirmation of whether the merchant ever provided proof that a refund was actually issued. Please note that I dispute both : the transaction amount charged ; and the fact that the ordered product was never received. I request written response and documentation regarding this matter as soon as possible.

Complaint Summary Wells Fargo denied a fraud claim on approximately {$5000.00} in unauthorized XXXX transactions on my joint checking account, despite my reporting them within the XXXX window required by Wells Fargos own policy. Two representatives gave me inconsistent explanations for the denial, and the second refused to disclose the criteria used to deny the claim. Background I am a long-standing Wells Fargo customer with XXXX accounts linked to my profile, including the joint checking account at issue. On the night of XX/XX/year>, my wife flagged XXXX pending XXXX transactions on the account that neither of us recognized. When I reviewed the account history, I discovered XXXX unauthorized XXXX transactions in total approximately {$5000.00}, including roughly {$2000.00} in pending charges that single night. Reporting Timeline XX/XX/year> ( same night ) : I attempted to file claims through Wells Fargos online portal. The system caps online disputes at XXXX per session, so I called Wells Fargo by phone to report the remaining unauthorized transactions. XX/XX/year> : I called back to confirm that every transaction had been logged. I was told to expect a resolution by XX/XX/XXXX within XXXX business days. All transactions were reported well within the XXXX window Wells Fargos policy requires. The Denial The claim was denied. When I called for an explanation, I received XXXX inconsistent accounts : 1. First representative : Told me the denial was based on insufficient evidence of fraud, citing the fact that I had logged into the account during the period the charges occurred and therefore should have noticed them sooner. This is not a denial criterion stated in Wells Fargos published fraud policy. 2. Second representative ( XXXX, Claims Resolution Manager, Wells Fargo Claims Assistance Center ) : Refused to disclose the criteria used to deny the claim, stating that revealing the verbiage or determination factors could put our process at risk. He acknowledged the account-login factor but could not confirm what other factors applied or whether the first representatives explanation was accurate. Lack of Recourse XXXX confirmed on a recorded call that the deciding department the High Dollar Fraud department has no inbound phone number. Customers can not call this department directly or be transferred to it. The only available step is to request a callback through a frontline representative, with no transparency into the criteria being applied. Both of my calls with Wells Fargo about this matter were recorded with my knowledge. Resolution Requested 1. Full reimbursement of the approximately {$5000.00} in unauthorized transactions. 2. A written explanation of the specific criteria Wells Fargo used to deny the claim, including how those criteria are consistent with Regulation E and Wells Fargos published fraud policy. 3. Disclosure of a direct contact method for the High Dollar Fraud department or its equivalent escalation path. Note for the Record The practice of denying fraud claims based on undisclosed internal criteria, from a department customers have no ability to contact directly, is a structural concern that almost certainly affects other Wells Fargo customers in similar circumstances. I am submitting this complaint not only to seek resolution for my own account, but to document the pattern.

CFPB Complaint Bank of America : Autopay Failure, Failure to Deliver Required Billing Statements, and Resulting Credit Harm I am filing this complaint against Bank of America regarding a series of failures that resulted in delinquencies on my credit report and significant credit harm, stemming directly from the banks failure to deliver billing statements as required by law. 1. Autopay Setup Failure I set up autopay through the Bank of America mobile application. During setup, the application experienced repeated crashes. After persisting through these failures, I received in-app confirmation that autopay had been successfully established. Despite this confirmation, payments were not processed, resulting in two delinquent payments totaling approximately {$60.00}. 2. Failure to Deliver Required Billing Statements Bank of America is legally required under the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) and Regulation Z to deliver periodic billing statements to cardholders. Bank of America failed to deliver these statements neither by U.S. mail nor by email for the billing cycles in question. As a result, I had no visibility into the missed payments and no opportunity to correct them. I only became aware of the delinquencies when they appeared on my credit report. When I raised this with Bank of America, representative XXXX XXXX stated that the bank could confirm statements had been sent, but when I requested documentation as proof, she was unable to provide it. A second representative on the escalations and collections team, XXXX [ last name unknown ], explicitly refused to furnish proof, stating outright that he would not do so despite indicating the information was accessible to him. The bank has no proof of delivery because the statements were not sent. XXXX. Credit Limit Reduction Bank of America reduced my credit limit significantly. While the reduction itself is not my primary concern, it was made on the basis of delinquencies that I was never informed of delinquencies I could and would have immediately resolved had I received the statements I was legally owed. The reduction is therefore a direct consequence of Bank of Americas own failure. 4. Missed Opportunity for Resolution XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXr I was contacted by a Bank of America XXXX XXXX XXXXalth manager soliciting me to move accounts. During that call, I raised the credit limit reduction. He committed to investigating and following up. He never called back. Had he done so, the underlying delinquency issue could have been identified and corrected promptly, preventing further credit harm. XXXX. Inconsistent Information and Unresolved Status Across multiple calls, I have received conflicting information from different Bank of America representatives regarding resolution timelines and applicable policies. I have paid late fees under protest, as the delinquency resulted from a confirmed autopay failure on Bank of Americas platform combined with their failure to deliver required statements.

input.narrative: Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau : I am writing to file a formal complaint against Summitt A * R, a debt collection company, for engaging in the unlawful practice commonly known as " debt parking '' placing a derogatory collection account on my consumer credit report without first providing the federally mandated written debt validation notice required under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692g, and the Consumer Financial Protection Bureaus Regulation F ( 12 C.F.R. Part 1006 ). What Summitt A * R Did : Summitt A * R placed a collection account on my credit report, causing immediate harm to my credit score and financial standing. Prior to reporting this account, Summitt A * R failed to send me the required written validation notice within five ( 5 ) days of its initial communication, as mandated by 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( a ). I did not receive any written notice informing me of : ( XXXX ) the amount of the debt ; ( XXXX ) the name of the creditor ; ( XXXX ) my right to dispute the debt within 30 days ; ( XXXX ) that the debt would be assumed valid if not disputed ; or ( XXXX ) that I could request the name and address of the original creditor. By reporting the debt to credit bureaus before completing required disclosures, Summitt A * R strategically pressured me to pay a debt I had no meaningful opportunity to verify or dispute the hallmark of illegal debt parking. Applicable Law Violated : FDCPA 1692g : Requires debt collectors to provide a written validation notice within 5 days of initial contact, informing consumers of their right to dispute the debt. CFPB Regulation F ( 12 C.F.R. 1006.30 ( b ) ) : Explicitly prohibits debt collectors from furnishing information to a consumer reporting agency regarding a debt before speaking with the consumer or before mailing the validation notice and waiting a reasonable time for it to be received. FCRA 1681s-2 : Prohibits furnishers from reporting inaccurate information to credit bureaus, including accounts reported in violation of applicable law. Harm Suffered : A significant and unexplained drop in my credit score. Denial or unfavorable terms on credit applications. Emotional distress, XXXX and time spent investigating and addressing the unauthorized reporting. Deprivation of my federally protected right to receive, review, and dispute the alleged debt before it damaged my credit.

input.issue: Problem with a purchase shown on your statement
input.narrative: In XX/XX/XXXX, I was approached in XXXX XXXX by a promoter for XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX who gave me a scratch-off ticket indicating I had " won '' a prize. This was used to bring me into a timeshare sales presentation. During that process I was provided with complimentary meals, alcohol, and transportation. The promoter built an ongoing personal relationship with me and made representations about coaching retreats, business collaborations, and income opportunities connected to the property. I purchased an original timeshare membership and in XX/XX/XXXX was approached about an upgrade to XXXX XXXX XXXX at a purchase price of {$100000.00}. I authorized a {$6000.00} deposit on my Citibank credit card ( account ending XXXX ) as part of that transaction. I was pressured to sign and return documents within a short timeframe or lose a promised " free week '' incentive. Material financial obligations including a recurring annual maintenance fee were never disclosed to me in writing. A second credit inquiry was run on my account in XX/XX/XXXX by XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX without my clear authorization, after I had already been approved. Following that second inquiry, financing terms were changed without explanation. Beginning in XX/XX/XXXX I made repeated written attempts to resolve these issues directly with the merchant. My XX/XX/XXXX email was never acknowledged. I received no clear or complete response to my concerns despite multiple follow-up attempts over several months. In XX/XX/XXXX the merchant submitted a written response to the XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX Complaint No. XXXX ) in which they made the following admissions : ( 1 ) that their promoter 's activities " include offering scratch off tickets and other incentives to encourage travelers to take a tour, '' confirming the deceptive entry tactic used on me ; ( 2 ) that a recurring annual maintenance fee of approximately {$2400.00} was disclosed only verbally, and that it would be " impossible to show documentation of something verbally disclosed, '' confirming material terms were never put in writing before I was charged ; ( 3 ) that although their own rules state no business may be conducted on the premises, they " made an exception to the rule and allowed for this Addendum '' for retreat activity, directly contradicting their position that all business representations were unrelated to the sale. I filed a billing dispute with Citibank for the charge of {$1200.00} from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX dated XX/XX/XXXX, assigned Case ID XXXX. Citibank denied the dispute on the grounds that " documentation or facts provided do not support the billing error dispute claim. '' However, the merchant 's XXXX admissions described above were made on XX/XX/XXXX, after my original dispute was filed, and were therefore not part of my original submission. These are new material facts that directly support my claim. I have submitted a formal rebuttal to Citibank with this new evidence and have not received confirmation that the dispute has been reopened. The conditional credit previously issued has been reversed. I have never stayed at or used this timeshare. I did attempt to make a reservation for the promised bonus week before it expired, as the merchant represented that benefit as part of the sale, but I was unable to secure it. No services of any kind have ever been rendered to me in exchange for these charges. Please note that a related CFPB complaint ( XXXX, filed XX/XX/XXXX ) covering the same underlying transaction with XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX is currently open and documents the unauthorized credit inquiry, changed financing terms, and undisclosed payment requirements by the same merchant. On XX/XX/year>, I mailed a formal written debt validation and verification request disputing the alleged debt in its entirety pursuant to the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ). In my request, I specifically demanded competent evidence establishing : * ownership of the alleged debt, * legal authority to collect, * complete itemization of the alleged balance, * full payment history, * chain of assignment, * bill of sale, * forward flow agreement, * transfer agreements, and * documentation showing whether XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX purchased the account or was merely collecting on behalf of another entity. Instead, the company only provided : * an alleged contract, * a partial payment ledger that does not reconcile with or explain the alleged balance of {$4400.00}, and * unrelated information belonging to another consumer identified as XXXX XXXX. I did not receive : * a complete accounting of how the alleged balance was calculated, * payment itemization, * principal/interest/fees breakdown, * charge-off calculations, * chain of title documentation, * bill of sale, * assignment records, * forward flow agreement, * transfer agreements, * proof of ownership, or * proof establishing whether the collector or another entity owns the account. The disclosure of another consumers information is extremely concerning and appears to demonstrate improper handling and commingling of consumer files and records. The company also failed to clearly identify whether : XXXX. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX actually owns the alleged account, or XXXX. Javitch Block LLC is simply attempting to collect on behalf of another entity. I believe the companys actions may violate : * FDCPA 15 U.S.C. 1692g for failure to provide proper validation, * FDCPA 15 U.S.C. 1692e for false, deceptive, or misleading representations, * FDCPA 15 U.S.C. 1692f for unfair collection practices, * FCRA 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 regarding accuracy and investigation obligations if information is being furnished to consumer reporting agencies, and * additional federal and state consumer protection laws regarding improper disclosure of consumer information. I am requesting that the CFPB require the company to : XXXX. Provide full competent validation of the alleged debt ; XXXX. Provide complete payment and balance itemization ; XXXX. Provide chain of assignment and ownership documentation ; XXXX. Explain the improper disclosure of another consumers information ; XXXX. Cease collection activity until lawful validation is provided ; XXXX. Cease furnishing inaccurate or unverifiable information to any consumer reporting agencies ; and XXXX. input.issue: Attempts to collect debt not owed
input.narrative: I am filing this complaint against XXXX for multiple violations of my federally protected rights under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq., in connection with an unrecognized account reported by Zion Debt Holdings ( Account ending XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX amount reported : {$3100.00} ). I have no knowledge of this account. I have never entered into any agreement with Zion Debt Holdings, never conducted any business with them or any original creditor they claim to represent, and never opened, authorized, or acknowledged any account associated with this alleged debt. This account does not belong to me. Additionally I am locked out of seeing the dispute results online getting an error message to " try again later ''. Lastly, I created a new consumer statement on XX/XX/XXXX to reflect what is currently happening and it was replaced with a previous consumer statement from XXXX. I am reporting the following sequence of events, each of which represents a serious concern : 1. UNAUTHORIZED DISPUTE CANCELLATION On XX/XX/XXXX, I submitted a formal written dispute to XXXX regarding the Zion Debt Holdings account. On the morning of XX/XX/XXXX, I received an email notification from XXXX stating that my request to cancel the dispute had been received. I did not submit any cancellation request not online, not by phone, not in writing, and not through any third party. Someone cancelled my dispute without my knowledge or authorization. This is a direct violation of my rights under FCRA 611 ( 15 U.S.C. 1681i ), which guarantees my right to dispute inaccurate information and have it reinvestigated. 2. PORTAL LOCKOUT FOLLOWING UNAUTHORIZED CANCELLATION After discovering the unauthorized cancellation, I attempted to refile my dispute through XXXX 's online portal. I was informed that XXXX only permits one dispute every 30 days. Because an unauthorized party cancelled my active dispute, I am now locked out of XXXX XXXX online dispute system for 30 days through no fault of my own. The FCRA imposes no such waiting period between disputes this is XXXX 's internal policy, and its application in this circumstance has effectively denied me my federally protected right to dispute. This 30-day lockout, triggered by an unauthorized cancellation, appears to be a deliberate interference with my consumer rights. 3. REPORTING OF UNVERIFIED ZOMBIE DEBT Zion Debt Holdings is a debt buyer that appears to have purchased this alleged debt as part of a bulk portfolio with little to no original documentation. Despite this, XXXX continues to report this unverified account on my credit file. XXXX 's reinvestigation process relies heavily on the automated e-OSCAR system, which allows furnishers to electronically confirm disputed accounts without producing any actual documentation. This does not constitute a reasonable investigation under the FCRA. I am requesting that the CFPB : 1. Investigate the unauthorized cancellation of my dispute and determine who submitted it and through what channel 2. Investigate XXXX 's 30-day portal lockout policy and its impact on consumers ' federally protected dispute rights 3. Require XXXX to immediately reinstate my dispute and begin a full reinvestigation 4. Require XXXX and Zion Debt Holdings to produce actual documentation proving this debt belongs to me 5. Direct XXXX to delete this account immediately if proper documentation can not be provided 6. Take any additional enforcement action warranted by the facts I am retaining all correspondence, including the unauthorized cancellation email, as evidence and am prepared to pursue all available legal remedies if this matter is not resolved promptly. Desired Resolution : Immediate reinstatement of my dispute, full reinvestigation, and deletion of the Zion Debt Holdings account from my XXXX credit file with written confirmation of that deletion.

input.narrative: We purchased a new XXXX XXXX XXXX ( VIN XXXX ) in XXXX of XXXX. We financed the car through Kia Finance America. The terms of the loan were for 48 months. The payment amount was set by the Kia Finance. All payments were made on time as we had set these up to be deducted from our checking account. In XX/XX/XXXX, we made our last payment. However, over two years later, when recently trying to sell our car, we learned we had a lien on our vehicle and a balance owed of {$65.00}. We received no notification in two years that we owed money and believed that we had satisfied our obligation in making all of the monthly payments on time, as per the terms of the loan. When I reached out to Kia Financial, I immediately paid the balance plus the interest that had accrued ( the final total was XXXX ). However, this did not immediately release the lien and it had taken an additional 2 weeks to receive notification that the lien was released. Today, nearly 3 weeks later, I am still not able to obtain a title without a lien from Kia Motors Finance from my Secretary of State 's office. All of this has occurred after we satisfied the terms of the loan and reasonably concluded the car had been paid off. Kia Finance made no effort in over two years to notify us that there was a balance. When I requested that the release be expedited, I was informed I would have to wait the standard amount of time. This was in speaking over the phone with Kia Finance This has created significant delays in the purchase of our next car. I reached out to XXXX XXXX XXXX, the parent company of Kia Finance, over a week ago via their website and have received no response from their customer services, aside from an automated response that they would reach out " soon ''. I was at my DMV this morning and there is still a lien on our vehicle 's title. I have not encountered this situation with other auto loan services in the past and am very disappointed in the lack of service recovery on the part of Kia Finance and XXXX XXXX. Thankfully, because we are trading our car in, and because the dealership will be satisfied with a release letter ( which again took nearly two weeks to receive ) this has not resulted in further harm but rather, delays and significant stress that should have been avoidable. I certainly would like to help prevent others from experiencing the stress or potential harm this has created for us. Further, had we been selling our car privately, we would not be able to provide a clean title as a result of this, for a car we understood to be paid off over two years ago.

input.issue: Applying for a mortgage or refinancing an existing mortgage
input.narrative: Unauthorized / Excessive Credit Inquiries and Misrepresentation of Credit Pulls I am filing this complaint regarding multiple credit inquiries that occurred during my interaction with Lennar Mortgage in connection with a potential home purchase inquiry. During the process, I was specifically advised that my information would be used for soft credit inquiries or review purposes only. However, after reviewing my credit reports, I discovered multiple hard inquiries were placed on my credit profile instead. At no point was it clearly explained to me that numerous hard inquiries would be conducted, nor was I properly informed of the potential impact these inquiries could have on my credit profile and mortgage shopping ability. Had I been accurately informed, I would have made a different decision regarding authorization. As a result, my credit profile was negatively impacted by excessive mortgage-related inquiries that I believe were either improperly disclosed or beyond what was reasonably necessary for the transaction. I am requesting : A full investigation into the credit inquiries associated with my application Documentation showing when and how authorization was obtained for each inquiry Review and removal of any unauthorized, excessive, duplicate, or improperly disclosed hard inquiries Confirmation of which entities accessed my credit report and why multiple pulls were necessary I also request that Lennar Mortgage review the manner in which information was presented to consumers regarding soft versus hard inquiries to ensure future applicants are properly informed before consent is obtained. I attempted to proceed through the homebuying process in good faith and expected transparency throughout the lending process. Unfortunately, the handling of my credit information has caused unnecessary stress and potential damage to my credit standing. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

A Kia Finance supervisor later confirmed to me on a recorded phone line that Kia chose to completely withhold digital notifications : they left XXXX voicemails, sent XXXX emails, and posted nothing to my online account portal to alert me that my account protection was removed. Because of this total lack of communication, I was left under the false impression that my account was safe and up to date under the approved deferral. On the current month, I was only 7 days past due. Because Kia 's system quietly reversed the deferral without notice, the system backdated my delinquency and executed a repossession on my vehicle around XXXX XXXX on XX/XX/2026. Relying on calls from numbers flagged by cellular networks as spamwhile intentionally refusing to leave voicemails or send digital lettersdoes not constitute a good-faith effort to notify a consumer of a default emergency. input.issue: Problems at the end of the loan or lease
input.narrative: I am submitting this complaint regarding Ally Financials handling of the insurance proceeds related to a totaled leased vehicle and its refusal to provide a transparent accounting regarding the application of those proceeds under the lease agreement. I leased a XXXX XXXX XXXX in XX/XX/XXXX through Ally Financial. The vehicle was later declared a total loss following an accident. The insurance carrier handling the claim was XXXX XXXX XXXX. Prior to the insurance company issuing payment, I directly contacted Ally Financial and requested a payoff amount for the lease. On XX/XX/XXXX, Ally Financial provided me with a written payoff amount of {$30000.00}. Afterward, XXXX XXXX initially offered a settlement amount of approximately {$33000.00}. I disputed the valuation, and the settlement amount was ultimately increased to {$36000.00}. During discussions with XXXX XXXX claim adjuster, I was advised that once XXXX XXXX received the payoff from Ally Financial, any difference between the payoff amount and the settlement amount would be sent to me. However, I later learned that Ally Financial, through XXXX, allegedly did not provide XXXX XXXX with an actual payoff statement. Instead, XXXX XXXX received a Letter of Guarantee requesting that the entire settlement amount of {$36000.00} be remitted to Ally Financial. I subsequently contacted Ally Financial and requested an explanation as to why the full settlement amount was retained despite the prior payoff quote of approximately {$30000.00}. Ally Financial advised me that pursuant to Section 39 of the lease agreement, it was entitled to retain the insurance proceeds. My concerns are as follows : 1. Ally Financial never provided me with a transparent accounting showing how the insurance proceeds were applied under Section 39 of the lease agreement. 2. Ally Financial never provided XXXX XXXX with what appears to have been a traditional payoff statement despite previously providing me with a payoff amount substantially lower than the final insurance settlement. 3. Ally Financial appears to have learned the exact settlement amount from the insurance company and then requested the entire settlement amount rather than disclosing the actual payoff/accounting calculation. 4. The lease agreement references credits, adjusted lease balances, unearned rent charges, prepaid depreciation, and potential refunds where credits exceed amounts due, yet Ally Financial has refused to provide a detailed reconciliation or ledger explaining why no refund was owed. 5. I believe Ally Financials handling of this matter lacked transparency and may constitute unfair or deceptive consumer financial practices. I am requesting the following : * A full accounting ledger and reconciliation under Section 39 of the lease agreement * Documentation showing how the insurance proceeds were applied * Copies of communications relating to the payoff demand * Clarification as to why the entire insurance settlement amount was retained despite the prior payoff quote * Investigation into whether Ally Financials practices regarding leased vehicle total loss settlements are compliant with applicable consumer protection laws If Ally Financial retained insurance proceeds in excess of amounts properly due under the lease agreement, I request reimbursement of those funds and any related amounts resulting from Ally Financial 's unjust enrichment I respectfully request that this matter be reviewed and investigated. XXXX XXXX

Since the opening of this account, I have consistently made timely payments and complied with all agreed-upon terms and obligations. My records, including account statements and payment confirmations, demonstrate responsible account management and do not support the reported late payment history. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), I am formally disputing this inaccurate reporting. Pursuant to 15 U.S.C. 1666 regarding correction of billing errors, consumers have the right to dispute inaccurate account reporting, and the reported late payments appear to constitute such errors. Additionally, 15 U.S.C. 1666a requires furnishers to properly investigate disputed information and avoid inaccurate reporting during the dispute process. Furthermore, FCRA 611 ( 15 U.S.C. 1681i ) provides consumers the right to dispute inaccurate information with consumer reporting agencies, while FCRA 623 ( a ) ( 2 ) and FCRA 623 ( b ) require furnishers to investigate disputed information and correct or update any inaccurate reporting.

A clear explanation of why Ally did not provide a workable registration solution before the vehicle had to be returned. XXXX. Reconsideration of the {$22000.00} balance as a hardship-driven and servicing-related outcome, rather than a voluntary early termination. XXXX. Reduction or waiver of the remaining lease payment liability and related fees caused by this unresolved registration issue. XXXX. Removal, correction, or suppression of any negative credit reporting or collection action related to this account while the dispute remains unresolved. Allys response does not adequately address the servicing failure that led to this outcome. Credit ACPT -AUTO LOAN IS NOT MINE I HAVE MADE COMPANY AWARE ACCOUNT ENDING XXXX XX/XX/year> To Whom It May Concern : I am in receipt of your XX/XX/year> response regarding the above-referenced account. The burden remains on Credit Acceptance to demonstrate that I knowingly entered into the agreement and that the signature is authentic. The IP address, device information, timestamps, geolocation data, and audit trail associated with the alleged electronic signature. XXXX. Any recorded communications, drivers license copies, identification documents, or biometric verification used during the transaction. XXXX. Documentation demonstrating that I personally reviewed and electronically signed the contract. XXXX. A complete chain of assignment and ownership of the alleged account. Until such evidence is produced, I maintain that the account remains disputed and unverified. Furthermore, under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, furnishers of information have a duty to conduct a reasonable investigation of disputed information. A document containing an alleged signature that I expressly deny does not conclusively establish liability or accuracy. Accordingly, I demand that Credit Acceptance : * Immediately mark the account as disputed with all consumer reporting agencies; * Conduct a reasonable reinvestigation of the account; * Cease reporting inaccurate information ; and * Remove this account from my consumer credit reports if you can not provide competent evidence that I personally authorized the transaction. Please consider this a formal notice that I continue to dispute the validity, ownership, and accuracy of this account. If Credit Acceptance continues reporting this account without conducting a reasonable investigation into my signature dispute, I reserve all rights available under federal and state law. I request a written response within 15 days of receipt of this correspondence. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX

I am filing this complaint against Bank of America ( BofA ) due to unreasonable delays, gross underwriting incompetence, and poor communication during a residential mortgage application, which severely jeopardized my real estate purchase, placed my {$10000.00} earnest money deposit at risk, and threatened a locked interest rate. Timeline and Amounts : XXXX 2026 : I applied for a {$600000.00} mortgage for a {$750000.00} residential property. I locked in a 5.375 % interest rate on a 7/6 ARM, which is valid until XX/XX/year>. XX/XX/year> : This was the original, legally binding closing date ( Close of Escrow ) established in the residential purchase contract. XX/XX/year> ( XXXX day before closing ) : BofAs underwriting team halted the issuance of the Final Closing Disclosure ( CD ). The delay was caused by the underwriter 's inability to understand standard real estate transaction documents regarding seller credits. The Core Issue and Bank 's Actions : The underwriting team created an artificial roadblock by conflating two legally distinct financial credits in the purchase contract : A {$5000.00} Seller Concession negotiated explicitly in lieu of physical property repairs. A {$14000.00} pass-through Broker Rebate. The seller agreed to fund a standard 2.5 % Buyer Broker Compensation ( {$18000.00} ). My broker retained their flat fee and legally rebated the remaining {$14000.00} to me to be applied toward closing costs. Despite having the executed Commission Disbursement Form and contract addendums clearly outlining these separate terms, the BofA underwriter erroneously claimed the {$14000.00} broker rebate violated the {$5000.00} limit placed strictly on the repair concessions. Because of the bank 's refusal to accurately read the contract and distinguish between a direct seller repair credit and a broker rebate, BofA refused to issue the Clear to Close. My Actions to Resolve the Issue : I responded immediately to every request. To satisfy the underwriter 's confusion, I was forced to draft and execute multiple emergency addendums with the seller at the absolute last minute ( on XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/year> ). These addendums explicitly spelled out the breakdown of the {$5000.00} seller concession versus the {$14000.00} broker rebate, exactly as the bank requested. The Impact and Harm : Because of Bank of Americas internal delays and failure to process standard real estate documents competently : I was forced to execute a contract extension, moving the closing date from XX/XX/year>, to XX/XX/year>. I was placed in a position of potential breach of contract with the seller, risking the forfeiture of my {$10000.00} earnest money deposit. I am filing a complaint regarding my auto loan account # XXXX involving Regional Acceptance Corporation and Truist. I believe I was placed into a financially unsustainable subprime auto loan despite obvious affordability concerns and financial hardship. At the time I obtained this loan, I was already upside down on a previous vehicle that I desperately needed to trade because it was unreliable and had structural damage issues that I did not fully understand until later. The dealership knew the vehicle was not worth what I owed on it, yet the negative equity was rolled into my current loan in order to complete the financing. I needed transportation and felt I had very limited options. I actually financed approximately {$22000.00}, yet after more than two years of payments my current principal balance is still {$27000.00}. My current 20-day payoff amount is {$34000.00} with daily interest charges of {$14.00} per day. The vehicle itself is worth significantly less than the loan balance. Since late 2024, I have repeatedly contacted Regional Acceptance and Truist requesting hardship assistance, payment reduction, restructuring, or temporary accommodations due to illness, unemployment, loss of income, and severe personal hardship. I recently started a new job and completed training, but I will not receive a full paycheck for another two weeks. Despite demonstrating financial hardship and actively communicating with the lender, I was informed there are essentially no hardship programs available to help reduce or temporarily adjust my payments. I do not understand why no meaningful hardship accommodation exists despite documented loss of income and my repeated efforts to avoid default. I rely on this vehicle to maintain employment and financial stability. I am not refusing to pay this debt. I am attempting to avoid repossession and continue making payments while trying to recover financially. I also later discovered that the vehicle I previously traded in had a history of structural damage from a major accident prior to my ownership. I did not fully become aware of the extent of this issue until the trade-in process in XXXX XXXX. The diminished value of that vehicle significantly contributed to the negative equity that was rolled into my current loan. While researching my situation, I found a very large number of publicly reported complaints from consumers describing similar experiences involving high-interest subprime loans, excessive balances compared to vehicle values, aggressive collections, and difficulty obtaining hardship assistance. After sending a detailed written hardship request to Regional Acceptance/Truist explaining my financial hardship, loss of income, new employment, and request for assistance, I received only a brief response directing me to call a general phone number without addressing my concerns regarding hardship accommodations, payment restructuring, or my account balance concerns. I feel my situation has not been meaningfully reviewed despite my repeated attempts to communicate in good faith. I am requesting a review of the loan servicing practices, hardship handling, account management, interest structure, and overall fairness of this loan situation. I am also requesting consideration for any available hardship accommodations or restructuring options that would allow me to continue working and responsibly address this debt.

input.narrative: I. INTRODUCTION I hereby submit this formal request for supervisory and administrative review of my federal student loan account in connection with my eligibility for XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ), voluntary payments made during the XXXX administrative forbearance period, and entitlement to borrower-favorable corrective relief. This request is made based on my proximity to XXXX discharge eligibility and the substantial payments made under conditions of administrative disruption and evolving program guidance. ________________________________________ II. FACTUAL BACKGROUND My account currently reflects 118 of 120 qualifying XXXX payments During the XXXX administrative forbearance period, I made 47 voluntary payments totaling approximately {$14000.00} These payments were made in good faith while actively pursuing XXXX eligibility The payments occurred during a period characterized by administrative uncertainty, program implementation changes, and evolving borrower guidance I am currently two qualifying payments from XXXX discharge eligibility Given these facts, there is a substantial likelihood that some or all these payments were not necessary to achieve forgiveness eligibility, resulting in potential overpayment and financial harm. ________________________________________ XXXX. REQUESTED RELIEF I respectfully request that the following forms of relief be evaluated concurrently and, on a borrower, -favorable basis : Primary Relief Immediate review for XXXX discharge eligibility, including application of any administrative mechanisms necessary to reach 120 qualifying payments Alternative Relief Refund of voluntary payments made during XXXX administrative forbearance ( approximately {$14000.00} ) Further Alternative Relief Corrective account adjustment, including : o XXXX payment count reconsideration o XXXX Buyback ( if applicable ) o Administrative correction sufficient to achieve XXXX eligibility ________________________________________ XXXX. BASES FOR RELIEF A. Payments Made During Administrative Forbearance The payments at issue were made during a period of administrative forbearance under the XXXX program. I request full review of all refund eligibility and corrective options applicable to payments made under these conditions. B. Potential Overpayment Given that I am currently at 118 qualifying payments, the 47 voluntary payments made during forbearance raise a clear question of whether amounts paid exceeded what was reasonably necessary to obtain XXXX discharge. C. Financial Harm The payments total approximately {$14000.00} and represent a material financial burden. To the extent these payments were unnecessary, I have experienced avoidable financial harm. D. Detrimental Reliance These payments were made in good-faith reliance on loan servicing and repayment expectations. I was not clearly advised that continued voluntary payments during this period may not be required or may later be subject to refund or correction. E. Administrative Disruption and Borrower Prejudice The XXXX implementation period involved changing guidance, processing delays, and servicing uncertainty. I request that my case be evaluated considering these conditions and that I not be disadvantaged by administrative transition outside my control. F. Equitable Considerations To the extent retention of these payments without review or relief would result in inequitable outcomes, I request borrower-favorable equitable correction to restore me to the position I reasonably would have occupied absent such disruption. ________________________________________

I am submitting this complaint regarding my mortgage servicer, XXXX XXXX XXXX, and lender, Acra Lending. As a result, I have struggled to keep up with my monthly mortgage payment of {$4900.00}. I have provided every document requested in a timely manner and have maintained records of all documents submitted. However, each time I am informed that my mortgage assistance package is complete, I am later contacted and asked to provide additional documentation. This repeated cycle has significantly delayed the review process and has made it difficult to move forward toward a resolution. The assistance I am requesting is intended to provide temporary relief while my family recovers financially. My goal is to obtain a more affordable monthly payment and a reduction in my current interest rate, which is extremely high. I am not seeking to avoid my obligations ; rather, I am trying to work with the company to establish a manageable payment arrangement so that I can continue making payments and avoid losing my home. I am also willing to accept other reasonable alternatives, including having the missed payments added to the end of the loan term so that I can bring the loan current and resume making regular monthly payments moving forward. My primary goal is to get back on track and keep my mortgage in good standing while my family recovers from this temporary hardship. At this time, I am approximately three months behind on my mortgage. I have been advised that once an account reaches this stage, the full delinquent amount must be paid or foreclosure proceedings may begin. This has placed tremendous stress on my family. I have two daughters and am working as hard as possible to improve our financial situation while pursuing every available option to keep our home. I am also working with a XXXX-approved housing counselor to navigate the mortgage assistance process. Despite these efforts, I have found customer service representatives at XXXX XXXX XXXX to be unhelpful and, at times, disrespectful during our communications. Rather than assisting me through the process, I often feel that unnecessary obstacles are being placed in the way of obtaining assistance. As of today, I have submitted all documentation that has been requested and am waiting to hear whether my file will be forwarded to underwriting for review. I am concerned that after months of providing documents and attempting to cooperate in good faith, my request may still be denied, leaving my family with few or no options to avoid foreclosure. I respectfully request that the company conduct a fair and timely review of my mortgage assistance application, communicate clearly regarding any remaining requirements, and work with me to identify a reasonable solution. Whether through a loan modification, a reduction in my monthly payment, a lower interest rate, or by moving the delinquent payments to the end of the loan term, I am simply seeking an opportunity to get current on my mortgage and keep my family in our home. Thank you for your time and consideration.

However, the reporting remains unchanged, and I have not received adequate proof validating the accuracy of the disputed information. Under 15 U.S.C. 1681i, credit reporting agencies must conduct a reasonable reinvestigation and delete or correct any information that can not be verified. In addition, any credit inquiries reported without proof of permissible purpose violate 15 U.S.C. 1681b and must be removed. Furnishers also have a duty under 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 to report complete and accurate account information. Late payments or derogatory marks reported without documentary support are inaccurate and misleading.
