input.product: Money transfer, virtual currency, or money service
input.narrative: Between XXXX XXXX XXXX, I purchased approximately {$30000.00} of the digital asset XXXX on Kraken. Before making these purchases, I conducted reasonable due diligence consistent with sound investing practices and Krakens own Terms of Service. I reviewed publicly available information about the project, including its website, documentation, and recent activity. At no point did I find any indication that a contract migration was underway. The only way I could have discovered the migration would have been to perform an extremely specific search such as active XXXX token migrationsomething no reasonable customer would know to do without being prompted. Kraken provided no such prompt or disclosure. I later learned that Kraken had platformrelevant knowledge as early as XX/XX/XXXX that XXXX deposits would be paused and that the token was under migration review. Kraken sent an email on XX/XX/XXXX only to customers who already held XXXX at that time. Because I had no prior XXXX holdings, I received no notice. Kraken has since acknowledged in writing that : I was not included in the XX/XX/XXXX communication, and No inplatform warning or pointofsale disclosure was displayed during the period when I made my purchases. As a result, I entered these transactions without material information that Kraken already possessed and that would have directly affected my decision to buy the asset. On XX/XX/XXXX, Kraken published migration details and snapshot dates, but this was after my purchases. The migration terms ( including a 90/10 allocation model and snapshot timing ) resulted in a significantly reduced allocation for customers like me who purchased during the undisclosed migration window. Kraken later introduced a second snapshot on XX/XX/XXXX, but this still did not make me whole relative to what I purchased. I contacted Kraken multiple times requesting clarification and resolution. Kraken eventually confirmed the communication timeline and admitted that no pointofsale disclosure was provided. However, they declined to offer compensation, citing their Terms of Service. The core issue is that Kraken failed to disclose material information at the poin t of sale, despite having exclusive, timesensitive knowledge of an active migration. This lack of disclosure prevented me from making an informed decision and caused financial harm. Please note that I am not disputing the XXXX project teams actions, the migration mechanics, or the allocation model they implemented. My complaint is solely about Krakens failure to provide pointofsale disclosure of material information that Kraken already possessed. The issue is not the migration itself, but the fact that I was allowed to purchase the asset during an active migration window without any notice, prompt, or warning that such a migration was underway. I also want to note that I was not expecting investment advice from Kraken, nor was I relying on Kraken to evaluate the merits of the XXXX project or its migration. My expectation ( any reasonable consumer ) was simply that Kraken would provide a basic factual notification of a significant, platformrelevant event that was already underway and known internally. Without such a notification, there was no reasonable way for me to know that a migration was in progress, and no reasonable consumer would think to search for something as specific as active XXXX token migration without being prompted. My concern is strictly about the absence of this pointofsale disclosure. I am requesting CFPB review of Krakens failure to provide clear and timely disclosures related to a material change affecting the asset I purchased.

input.issue: Problems at the end of the loan or lease
input.narrative: I am filing this complaint against Premier Auto Credit for refusing to honor a signed settlement agreement. On XX/XX/XXXX, Premier Auto Credit provided me with a written settlement agreement concerning my vehicle loan for a XXXX XXXX XXXX. The agreement stated that my outstanding balance was {$7400.00} and that Premier Auto Credit agreed to accept {$3500.00} as full and final payment of the account. The agreement further stated that upon satisfaction of the payment requirements, I would be released from all liability under the contract. The settlement agreement was signed by both Premier Auto Credit and me on XX/XX/XXXX. At the time Premier Auto Credit made and signed this settlement agreement, my vehicle had already been involved in an accident and had already been determined to be a total loss. After learning that insurance proceeds would be available, Premier Auto Credit informed me that it would no longer honor the signed settlement agreement and instead demanded approximately {$7500.00}, which is essentially the full loan balance. The written settlement agreement contains no language stating that the agreement is void if insurance is involved, no language permitting Premier Auto Credit to revoke the agreement after execution, and no language stating that the company may demand the full balance if an insurance claim exists. I believe Premier Auto Credit entered into a written settlement agreement and then attempted to withdraw that agreement solely because it became aware that insurance funds might be available. Because the vehicle was already a total loss before the settlement agreement was executed, Premier Auto Credit either knew or should have known the circumstances surrounding the vehicle before offering and signing the settlement. I relied on the signed agreement and expected Premier Auto Credit to honor its written terms. Refusing to honor the agreement after it was signed has caused financial hardship, uncertainty, and has prevented resolution of the account under the agreed terms. I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau investigate Premier Auto Credits actions, require the company to explain why it refuses to honor a signed settlement agreement, and determine whether its conduct violates consumer financial protection laws. I further request that Premier Auto Credit honor the written settlement agreement and accept the agreed settlement amount of {$3500.00} as full satisfaction of the account. I have attached a copy of the signed settlement agreement for review.

input.narrative: I am disputing an unauthorized electronic fund transfer under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( Regulation E ). The transfer was induced entirely by a phishing deception and fraudulent bank impersonation, meaning I did not give valid authorization. On XXXX I received a call from a Wells Fargo smart caller ID number saying they were from the fraud department and said there was a suspicious XXXX transfer from my checking account for {$3500.00} and they were going to help me get it refunded. After a long process, they somehow convinced me that I had to simulate a {$3500.00} payment to the thief to complete the refund process. When questioned, they assured me that the account was frozen an locked and that the transaction would not go through but had to be done to continue to get the refund. I did as told and of course it was a scam. I informed Wells Fargo fraud department that I was targeted by a phishing scam, that Wells Fargo failed to protect my account, and that they refused to perform a proper investigation or assist you when you reported it. Wells Fargo said it was not eligible for a fraud claim because I initiated the transfer, Even though I may have physically pressed the button to initiate the XXXX transfer, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) maintains that transfers induced by a scammer impersonating a bank employee or utilizing a high-level phishing trick do not constitute legal authorization by the consume The transaction violates Regulation E because my intent was defrauded by an impostor. Regulation E ( 12 CFR Part 1005 ), which protects consumers against unauthorized electronic fund transfers should apply to my case.

input.narrative: I am submitting this supplemental complaint regarding Premier Auto Credits refusal to honor a signed settlement agreement. On XXXX XXXX XXXX, Premier Auto Credit executed a written settlement agreement agreeing to accept {$3500.00} as full and final settlement of an account with a stated balance of {$7400.00}. The agreement was signed by both parties. After the agreement was executed, Premier Auto Credit informed me that it would not honor the settlement agreement and would instead demand the full balance. Premier Auto Credit has now stated in writing that it considers the agreement void due to alleged material non-disclosure because the vehicle had been involved in an accident and was the subject of an insurance claim. I dispute this position. During settlement negotiations, I requested a settlement of my account. I did not make any false statements or misrepresentations. Premier Auto Credit never asked whether the vehicle had been involved in an accident, whether an insurance claim existed, or whether the vehicle had been declared a total loss. The settlement agreement itself contains no provision requiring disclosure of an accident or insurance claim and no provision allowing Premier Auto Credit to revoke the agreement based on those facts. Premier Auto Credits position appears to be that I had an affirmative duty to volunteer information that was never requested. However, the company has not identified any provision of the settlement agreement, any provision of the underlying loan contract, or any specific legal authority that imposed such a duty. The timing of Premier Auto Credits actions is also concerning. The company agreed to accept {$3500.00} as full settlement, but after learning that insurance proceeds may be available, it withdrew the settlement and demanded approximately {$7500.00} instead. This creates the appearance that the company is attempting to obtain a greater recovery after entering into a written agreement. I respectfully request that the CFPB investigate Premier Auto Credits refusal to honor the signed settlement agreement, review whether its conduct complies with applicable consumer protection laws, and require the company to provide a detailed explanation and legal basis for its decision to revoke the agreement. As a fair resolution, I request that Premier Auto Credit honor the XXXX XXXX XXXX settlement agreement, accept the agreed settlement amount of {$3500.00} as full satisfaction of the account, release any remaining claimed deficiency balance, and provide a complete accounting of the loan and settlement dispute.

I have made consistent, on-time payments of {$420.00} throughout the life of my auto loan often paying ahead of my due date. Specifically : 1. From XX/XX/XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX, my account balance remained frozen at {$11000.00} across multiple payment cycles despite four payments of {$420.00} each. During this entire period, 100 % of my payments were applied to interest with {$0.00} applied to principal. 2. Following a payment processed on XX/XX/XXXX, my Next Due date advanced from XX/XX/XXXX to XX/XX/XXXX skipping two months entirely. This is consistent with a deferment or extension being applied to my account. 3. My payment history contains an unidentified transaction ( XXXX XXXX XXXX, effective XX/XX/XXXX ) for {$13000.00} applied entirely to principal, with no explanation provided. On XX/XX/XXXX, I submitted a formal written inquiry to the company requesting : ( 1 ) confirmation of whether a deferment or loan modification was placed on my account and the dates it was active, ( 2 ) documentation of my written authorization for any such modification, ( 3 ) explanation of unidentified transaction codes, ( 4 ) my current payoff amount and whether any deferred balance remains, and ( 5 ) a copy of my original signed retail installment contract. The company responded by sending only a copy of my payment history with no explanation, then followed up with a two-sentence email directing me to call their customer service line. As of XX/XX/XXXX 18 days after my written inquiry I have not received a substantive written response to any of my requests. This has resulted in a higher remaining loan balance, a potentially extended loan term, and credit impact I did not authorize. I am requesting that the CFPB require the company to provide a full written explanation of all account modifications and any corrective action warranted.
